rules.title: No clipped text
rules.text: Nothing a person needs to read ends in an ellipsis: names, panel titles, file names, button labels. Wrap to two lines or widen the container.

rules.title: No clipped controls
rules.text: No button, field or panel is cut by its container at any width from 360 to 1920 px. Panels scroll inside themselves before they overflow.

rules.title: No browser-default controls
rules.text: Selects, checkboxes, radios, ranges, number, date and file inputs, and text areas are styled by the kit, with a visible focus ring.

rules.title: Fields have a sensible width
rules.text: A text field is never wider than 480 px, except one search or formula bar. A form is one column, at most 640 px wide.
rules.threshold: field at most 480 px; form at most 640 px

rules.title: Content does not float in a void
rules.text: A screen that fills under half the window centres a reading column, fills the window, or shows an empty state with one action.

rules.title: One type scale
rules.text: Sizes come from the tokens only. Mono is for labels and status, never for a sentence.

rules.title: Spacing on the 4 px grid
rules.text: Spacing comes from the spacing tokens, so every gap and padding is a multiple of 4 px.

rules.title: Targets are big enough
rules.text: Every pointer target is at least 28 px, and at least 40 px on a phone. Tab order follows reading order and Esc closes the top layer.

rules.title: Every state is designed
rules.text: Loading, empty, error and denied each have a designed state. A blank rectangle is never one of them.

rules.title: Light and dark, phone and desktop
rules.text: Each screen works in both themes and at 390 by 844. On a phone, side panels become sheets or tabs.

rules.title: Plain words on screen
rules.text: Copy is plain sentence case and says what a person cares about. It never talks about how the app is built.

rules.title: Every control does something
rules.text: A button that does nothing is removed or made to work. A disabled control looks disabled and says why.

rules.title: Types pass
rules.text: The app type-checks with no errors.

rules.title: Tokens only
rules.text: Colours, sizes and spacing come from the kit tokens, never literal values.

rules.title: Only allowed dependencies
rules.text: Dependencies and their licences are on the allowlist. An outside pull request never changes the lockfile.

rules.title: No network or eval in source
rules.text: The source makes no network calls and uses no eval or dynamic code.

rules.title: No network or eval in the build
rules.text: The built bundle makes no network calls and uses no eval or dynamic code.

rules.title: Within the size limit
rules.text: The app and its assets stay within the published size limit.

rules.title: Opens cleanly in a browser
rules.text: The app opens at four sizes in light and dark, and any request to another origin fails the check.

rules.title: Accessible
rules.text: No serious or critical accessibility problems.

rules.title: One app folder only
rules.text: A pull request changes only the folder of its own app.

rules.title: Permissions stay inside the envelope
rules.text: The manifest asks only for permissions the program allows.

rules.title: Every declared permission is used
rules.text: A reviewer confirms each declared permission is needed for the app's one job.

rules.title: Manifest is complete and valid
rules.text: No placeholders, no reserved slugs, an id in the right namespace, a folder that matches, and a slug that is a valid DNS label.

rules.title: Owner matches the author
rules.text: The GitHub id in the manifest is the id of the person who opened the pull request.

rules.title: Commits are signed off
rules.text: Every commit carries a Signed-off-by line (DCO 1.1). A GitHub noreply address is fine.

rules.title: One clear job
rules.text: The app does one thing, and does what its summary says.

rules.title: Works with made-up data and is not a duplicate
rules.text: The app is useful with made-up data and does not repeat an app that is already listed.

rules.title: Content limits and no dark patterns
rules.text: Content stays within the published limits and nothing in the app pushes people into choices they did not mean to make.
